# v1.1.0-dev.62 — The Display editor tells you what it's going to do

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.61`.

The Display editor had three things in it that meant three
different things and looked identical. Two of them have moved
out, and what's left opens with a plain sentence about what
loading the profile will actually change.

## It Says What It Will Do

The top of the editor now reads something like:

```
When you press Ctrl+Alt+3
  Left 4K        150%, and 2560 × 1440 @ 60 Hz from your PC-wide 150% rule
  Right 1080p is left alone.
  Then 6 windows go back to their saved places.
```

It's built from the same settings the Save button writes, so it
can't tell you one thing and do another. When a resolution comes
from one of your PC-wide rules rather than from the profile, it
says so, which is the only honest way to explain that a profile
setting a zoom level can also change your resolution.

## Your Displays Have Names Now

Windows reports "Generic PnP Monitor" for very nearly every
monitor ever made, so three displays used to show three identical
rows. They're named by where they are and what they run now:
**Left 4K**, **Right 1080p**, **Left 1440p portrait**. A virtual
display says that it is one.

The same name is used in the summary and on the row, so it's
obvious which sentence is about which display.

## Zoom Rules Moved To Settings

The zoom to resolution table is now in **Settings → Auto-activation
→ Zoom to resolution rules**, next to the switch that already
turned this whole feature on and off.

It was in the per-profile editor, which was the wrong place and
actively misleading: it looked exactly like the profile's own
settings sitting right above it, but it applied to every profile
on the machine. People reasonably read it as belonging to the
profile they had open.

It's one table now, with the display named in every row, and a
**Matched by** column that tells you how each rule finds its
display. That last one matters if you use virtual displays,
because it's the difference between a rule that survives a
reconnect and one that doesn't.

## A Rule Could Land On The Wrong Monitor

Worth flagging on its own, because it would have bitten anyone
with two displays of the same model.

Rules are filed against a display's hardware identity. That
identity was the monitor *model*, which is stable but not unique:
two Parsec virtual displays are both "PSCCDD0", and so are two
identical monitors. A rule for one would have applied to the
other.

The key now includes which output the display is on, which is
also stable across reconnects. Same model, different screens,
different rules. Rules written before this still work.

## Parsec Registration Is Its Own Window

The **Parsec resolutions** button appears when a Parsec display
is connected. It writes to a driver, needs an administrator
prompt, and has nothing to do with the profile you happen to have
open, so it no longer sits inside that profile's editor.

## Smaller Things

- The editor doesn't scroll any more. Everything is reachable
  without moving.
- The explanatory paragraphs are gone. There were 185 words of
  them and they were mostly restating the labels underneath.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
